sounds.intro: Urdu is written right to left in an Arabic-based script. Short vowels are usually not written, so the Latin shown is how it is said. Spoken Urdu is almost the same as spoken Hindi. Every noun is masculine or feminine.
rows: a "k" made far back in the throat
aspirated: a puff of air after the sound
a nasal at the end of a word: the vowel is said through the nose
notes: Verbs and adjectives change for a man or a woman: -a for a man, -i for a woman (thaka = tired, man; thaki = tired, woman). This book shows the man's form.
The Latin is a common spelling for learners. Urdu has no standard Latin spelling.

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Three words for "you": tu (very close, rude to strangers), tum (friendly), aap (polite). Use aap when unsure. "Woh" means he, she, it and they, and "yeh" means this.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Masculine nouns ending in -a change to -e (larka, larke). Feminine nouns add -ein (kitaab, kitaabein) or -iyan (billi, billiyan). Many masculine nouns do not change (ghar, ghar).

grammar.title: To be: hoon, ho, hai
text: The verb "to be" has its own forms: hoon, ho, hai, hain. It comes at the end of the sentence.

grammar.title: Mere paas: have, there is
text: Urdu says "near me there is": mere paas ... hai. "Hai" means there is, "nahin hai" means there is not.

grammar.title: Present tense: -ta hoon
text: Verb stem + -ta + hoon / ho / hai / hain. A man says -ta, a woman says -ti. Aana (to come): aa-ta hoon.
ex: woh bank mein kaam karti hai
woh bank mayn kaam KUR-tee hai
وہ بینک میں کام کرتی ہے

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: The verb goes last. Order: who, where or when, what, verb. Urdu has no words for "a" or "the".

grammar.title: Negation
text: Put "nahin" before the verb "hai" or "hoon". Always compare with the positive form.
ex: I do not have a car
woh itwaar ko kaam karta hai
woh it-WAAR koh kaam KUR-taa hai
وہ اتوار کو کام کرتا ہے
he does not work on Sundays
woh itwaar ko kaam nahin karta
woh it-WAAR koh kaam na-HEEN KUR-taa
وہ اتوار کو کام نہیں کرتا

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Put "kya" at the start. The rest of the sentence does not change.
ex: kya yeh aap ki kitaab hai?
kyaa yeh aap kee ki-TAAB hai
کیا یہ آپ کی کتاب ہے؟
kya aap ko chai pasand hai?
kyaa aap koh chai pa-SUND hai
کیا آپ کو چائے پسند ہے؟

grammar.title: Question words
text: Question words stand where the answer would stand.

grammar.title: Possessives and liking
text: Mera (my), tumhara (your), uska (his / her), hamara (our), aap ka (your, polite). They agree with the thing owned: mera ghar, meri kitaab. To say you like something, use "mujhe ... pasand hai" (to me it is pleasing).
ex: مجھے فٹ بال بہت پسند ہے

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: tum (informal): friends, family, children. aap (formal): strangers, older people, work. The verb changes too: -ho (tum), -hain (aap).
rows: tum kaise ho? / aap kaise hain?
تم کیسے ہو؟ / آپ کیسے ہیں؟
tum bolte ho / aap bolte hain
تم بولتے ہو / آپ بولتے ہیں

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: gaya (went, man), gayi (went, woman). Future: -oonga (I will, man): main jaoonga. Women say -oongi.

grammar.title: Commands
text: The bare stem is the friendly command (aao, come). Add -iye for polite (aaiye). "Mat" before it forbids: mat aao.

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: Can: verb + sakta hoon (main tair sakta hoon). Must: "chahiye" or "hai" with -na (mujhe jaana hai). Want: chahta hoon (main khaana chahta hoon).
ex: kya aap meri madad kar sakte hain?
kyaa aap MAY-ree ma-DUD kar SUK-tay hain
کیا آپ میری مدد کر سکتے ہیں؟
I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: Urdu puts little words after the noun: mein (in), par (on, at), se (from), ko (to), ka / ke / ki (of).
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
the shop is next to the bank
the park is near the station
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Put "se" after the thing you compare with: us se bara (bigger than that). For "the most" say "sab se": sab se bara.
rows: bara, us se bara, sab se bara
بڑا، اس سے بڑا، سب سے بڑا
chhota, us se chhota, sab se chhota
چھوٹا، اس سے چھوٹا، سب سے چھوٹا

BUH-raa oos say BUH-raa sub say BUH-raa
